first_check.explanation: D.N.J. L.Civ.R. 26.1(b) is real, but it is titled 'Meeting of Parties, Discovery Plans, and Initial Disclosures.' It covers the Rule 26(f) meeting, the timing and contents of the discovery plan, and initial disclosures. It sets no requirements for privilege logs or privilege-log entries. second_check.explanation: The finding holds. The D.N.J. amendment order of September 30, 2016 gives L.Civ.R. 26.1(b) the heading '(b) Meeting of Parties, Discovery Plans, and Initial Disclosures'. Its text covers the Rule 26(f) meeting, the contents of the discovery plan (including '(g) Any orders, such as data preservation orders, protective orders, or orders reflecting agreements under Federal Rule of Evidence 502'), and the timing of initial disclosures. It says nothing about the form or contents of privilege logs. Saying that clawback privilege-log entries must 'conform to the requirements of ... Local Civil Rule 26.1(b)' therefore attributes requirements to the rule that it does not contain.
